name: Clarification pending → executing→awaiting_approval
description:
ADR-053 Phase 4b-2 — the interactive-pause transition, half 2 (the run-entity transition). Fires on the RUN entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>) when rule 07 or 08 has stamped agent.run.clarification_pending there AND the run is still `executing` AND no resume is in flight. Advances the run to `awaiting_approval` via lifecycle_transition (the firing entity = the run entity, which is what the action transitions). The run is now honestly paused on a human reply rather than misleadingly `executing`.

Mirrors 02-dispatched-to-executing.json exactly (marker trigger + top-level phase guard + lifecycle_transition). The executing→awaiting_approval edge is already legal in the upstream transition table (agentrun.go), so no lifecycle change.

PHASE GUARD IS A TOP-LEVEL CONDITION, NOT AN ACTION `when` (Coby review round 2): agent.run.phase==executing is a rule condition, so the rule is simply not-matching until the edge is legal — the illegal transition is never attempted and the durable clarification_pending marker re-drives the transition exactly once when the phase is executing (beta.103+ re-evaluates every entity-state rule per KV revision).

RESUME MUTUAL-EXCLUSION (PR-2, agent.run.clarification_resumed length_eq 0): this is the bounce-proof guard. Rule 10 stamps agent.run.clarification_resumed on the run the instant a clarification reply arrives, and rule 11 then transitions awaiting_approval→executing and removes BOTH markers (clarification_pending first, then clarification_resumed). Without this guard, rule 11's transition back to `executing` would briefly satisfy THIS rule's (clarification_pending + phase==executing) while clarification_pending is still being cleared → an infinite pause↔resume bounce. With it, this rule is structurally dead from the moment a resume starts until both markers are gone — at every intermediate KV revision EITHER clarification_resumed is still set (this guard blocks) OR clarification_pending is already removed (the first condition blocks). No atomic-write primitive needed; the ordering of rule 11's removes + this guard make the bounce impossible regardless of re-eval granularity.

SHARED PHASE WITH 4c: awaiting_approval is also 4c's tool-gate phase. They are distinguished by CAUSE, not phase: 4b-2 stamps agent.run.clarification_pending + the asking loop has coordinator.user_question and NO pending_approval; 4c's tool-gate sets pending_approval. The UI follow-up disambiguates on those triples.

DOES NOT collide with 03/04 (executing→completed/failed): a recovery coordinator's ask_user stamps clarification_pending but NOT agent.run.outcome, so rules 03/04 do not fire; and once the run is awaiting_approval their phase==executing guard excludes them.

on_enter.reason: coordinator asked the user a clarifying question — run paused awaiting reply (ADR-053 4b-2)

Rule 10 stamps clarification_resumed on resume; this guard makes pause structurally dead until rule 11 clears both markers, so rule 11's awaiting_approval→executing can never re-trip this rule (no pause↔resume bounce).
